name: Tool4That
description: Need a tool for that? Free single-file tools that run in your browser without sign-ups or tracking: personal finance calculators, a cybersecurity course with practice drills, hardening labs that run without a virtual machine, and creative experiments like a beat-making studio.

categories.title: Personal finance
categories.tagline: Max your TSP. See where your money goes.
categories.description: Calculators for your money: the exact myPay percentages to max your TSP without losing the match, and a personal finance advisor that reads your statements on your own device.
categories.note: Planning aids, not financial or tax advice. Nothing you enter leaves your browser.

categories.title: Cybersecurity
categories.tagline: Learn cyber defense, then drill it.
categories.description: Two ways in. Learning builds the concepts, from your first command to confident defender. Practice is hands-on reps: Net Drills for subnetting and Cisco IOS, Lockdown Drills for hardening Windows, Linux, FreeBSD, and Cisco IOS, and Lockdown Range for full hardening labs in your browser.
categories.note: Unofficial training, independent of and unendorsed by the makers of the systems it names. Defensive skills only: practice on machines you own or are authorized to use. Progress stays in your browser.

categories.title: Imagination Land
categories.description: Creative tools and one-off experiments that live outside the other categories. They gather here until there are enough of a kind to earn a category of their own.
categories.note: Everything runs in your browser, and what you make stays on your device.

sections.title: Learning
sections.intro: Build the concepts and vocabulary, from your first terminal command to confident defender. New to cybersecurity? Start with Defense Ladder, the course. Know what you need? The Study Map finds any concept as you type and shows where to learn and practice it. Command Atlas looks up any command in the course and shows what it does and where you use it. Cyber PUG gives a team experimental checklists for taking over a network, coordinated from a shared Collab Tab, with a Map that draws the network from pasted command output.

sections.title: Practice
sections.intro: Hands-on reps once you know the ideas. Net Drills are timed networking drills. Lockdown Drills walk you through hardening each system step by step. Lockdown Range drops you into a full simulated machine to harden on your own, with a live Progress Check.

series.title: Net Drills
series.description: Four networking drills: subnetting and IPv6, Cisco IOS configuration, config audits, and troubleshooting from real device output.
series.note: Unofficial training, independent of and unendorsed by the makers of the systems it names. Progress stays in your browser.

series.title: Lockdown Drills
series.description: Baseline-hardening trainers for Windows 11, Windows Server, the Debian family (Ubuntu and Linux Mint), FreeBSD, and Cisco IOS, each in three levels: Doorman, Watchman, and Hunter. A plain-text command reference explains why each step matters.
series.note: Unofficial training, independent of and unendorsed by the makers of the systems it names. Practice hands-on in the Lockdown Range and, on a real machine you own or are authorized to change, with Cyber PUG.

series.title: Lockdown Range
series.description: Full hardening labs that run in your browser without a virtual machine: Windows 11 and Windows Server, Ubuntu and Linux Mint, and a Packet Tracer-style Cisco topology. Each Range has three levels (Recruit, Operator, and Captain) plus Level 4 · Advanced · extra credit, which builds a different machine on every attempt and gives a layout code a class can share. One layout code works in all three Ranges, and each Range builds its own machine from it. Sign in, read the scenario brief, answer the investigation questions, fix the machine, and watch a live Progress Check.
series.note: Unofficial training, independent of and unendorsed by the makers of the systems it names. Simulated machines only: nothing touches your computer, and progress stays in your browser.

tools.name: Maxed & Matched TSP Calculator
tools.tagline: Hit the max. Keep the match.
tools.description: Your exact myPay TSP percentages, straight from your LES. Reach the IRS limit in your last paycheck without losing a dollar of BRS match.

tools.name: PFAT — Personal Finance Advisor Tool
tools.description: Add transactions by hand, paste text, or import CSV, PDF, and scanned statements or app screenshots. Get a money-in, money-out Home summary, a paycheck plan, a 30-day look ahead, and a plain-language checkup. Everything stays on your device.
tools.download_note: Both downloads are the full app. Download: reads PDFs and pictures when online. Download for offline use: reads PDFs, screenshots, and scanned statements on your device, completely offline.

tools.name: Defense Ladder
tools.tagline: Start here: the course, one grade at a time.
tools.description: A free, four-grade cybersecurity course, Freshman to Senior, built on Bloom's taxonomy: 51 units across Windows, Linux, networking, security foundations, defense operations, and web and cloud, with a readiness check at the start of Sophomore, Junior, and Senior. Diagrams, drills on realistic logs, captures, and configs, a pace planner, and a glossary round it out. Works offline, and everything stays in your browser.
tools.download_note: Each grade also comes as its own smaller download for offline use; links to other grades open the online course.

tools.name: Subnet Sprint
tools.description: Slide the mask in the sandbox and watch every value react, then work out network, broadcast, and host ranges against the clock. Includes VLSM planning and IPv6 drills.

tools.name: IOS CLI Lab
tools.description: Configure a simulated router and switch from their consoles, then prove it from two PCs. Timed missions, from the basics to VLAN trunks, router-on-a-stick, a Telnet filter, DHCP snooping, logging, time, and SSH access for the Teachers VLAN only.

tools.name: Config Audit
tools.description: Flag every risky line in a running-config, choose the best fix, and name the protections that are missing entirely. Four configs, including a Site B switch and router.

tools.name: Trouble Tickets
tools.tagline: Read the output. Find the fault.
tools.description: Study the complaint and real device output, then pick the root cause; every ticket ends with the fix. Log tickets add Windows, Linux, and Cisco logs: name what happened, then pick the command that surfaces it.

tools.name: Windows 11 Lockdown
tools.description: Windows 11 baseline hardening in three levels: Doorman, Watchman, and Hunter. A command reference explains why each step matters.

tools.name: Windows Server Lockdown
tools.description: Windows Server baseline hardening in three levels: Doorman, Watchman, and Hunter. A command reference explains why each step matters.

tools.name: Debian Family Lockdown
tools.tagline: Lock down Ubuntu and Linux Mint.
tools.description: Ubuntu and Linux Mint baseline hardening in three levels: Doorman, Watchman, and Hunter. A switch shows each distribution's steps, and a command reference explains why each step matters.

tools.name: FreeBSD Lockdown
tools.description: FreeBSD baseline hardening in three levels: Doorman, Watchman, and Hunter. A command reference explains why each step matters.

tools.name: Cisco IOS Lockdown
tools.description: Cisco IOS baseline hardening in three levels: Doorman, Watchman, and Hunter. A command reference explains why each step matters.

tools.name: Windows Range
tools.tagline: Harden the workstation. Then the server.
tools.description: Windows 11 and Windows Server 2025 hardening scenarios in your browser, in three levels (Recruit, Operator, and Captain) plus Level 4 · Advanced · extra credit, which builds a different machine on every attempt and gives a layout code a class can share. Sign in, read the scenario brief, answer the investigation questions, then fix each one with the real panels or the command line while a live Progress Check keeps count.

tools.name: Linux Range
tools.tagline: Harden the box from the shell.
tools.description: Ubuntu, Linux Mint, and Ubuntu Server in your browser, in three levels (Recruit, Operator, and Captain) plus Level 4 · Advanced · extra credit, which builds a different machine on every attempt and gives a layout code a class can share. A real-feeling bash terminal with sudo, apt, systemctl, ufw, PAM, cron, and nano. A live Progress Check also runs availability checks that flag any authorized user, administrator, or critical service you break.

tools.name: Cisco Range
tools.tagline: Secure the topology. Prove it with ping.
tools.description: A Packet Tracer-style topology in your browser: IOS consoles with ? help, abbreviations, and the exact error messages, plus PC command prompts. Three levels (Recruit, Operator, and Captain) run from one router to two switches joined by a trunk. Level 4 · Advanced · extra credit is a two-site school network with VLAN trunks, router-on-a-stick, and OSPF that builds a different Site B on every attempt and gives a layout code a class can share. A live Progress Check keeps count.

tools.name: Study Map
tools.tagline: Every concept: find it, learn it, practice it.
tools.description: Every concept in the cybersecurity course in one place. Type a concept and see the Defense Ladder unit that teaches it and the drills and labs that practice it, with a link to its commands in Command Atlas. Browse by topic, track, grade, network layer, or app. Rate what you know as Explore, Revisit, or Strong to get your own study path.

tools.name: Command Atlas
tools.tagline: Every command in the course: what it does and where you use it.
tools.description: Every command in the cybersecurity course on Windows, Linux, FreeBSD, and Cisco IOS in one place. Type a command or a task to see what it does, its options and arguments, every lesson, drill, and lab that uses it, the expected answers behind a reveal, and its vendor documentation. The Checklist map lists each Cyber PUG checklist step with its commands' first lesson, drills, and Range checks.

tools.name: Cyber PUG
tools.tagline: Experimental takeover checklists and a network Map, coordinated from a shared Collab Tab.
tools.description: Cyber PUG (Pick-Up Game): experimental team checklists for taking over a network. Windows, eight Unix-like families, and Cisco, with a shared Collab Tab. Paste command output under a checklist line, and the Map tab draws the network by site, VLAN, and subnet, lists leads to check, and compares before with after. Works offline.
tools.download_note: Open with photo reading (about 12 MB) also turns a photo or a screenshot of a terminal into text, right on your device. Both editions keep the same save on this site. Each download is the full page.

tools.name: Chop Lab
tools.description: A music studio in your browser: 16 pads, a step sequencer with patterns up to 128 bars, a song timeline for layering patterns into full tracks, a kit for each pattern, 63 genre kits from boom bap and house to jazz, reggae, country, and metal, a sample chopper, a Screw control that slows and deepens everything, two DJ decks with scratching, recording to WAV, and music packs of seamless MP3 loops.
